title: ChiroEcho: extending automated bat vocalisation classification beyond the learned taxonomy
abstract: arXiv:2608.18191v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Bats are key indicators of ecosystem health and are protected throughout Europe, making reliable population monitoring a conservation priority. Their cryptic nocturnal lifestyle makes passive acoustic monitoring essential, yet automated identification remains difficult as echolocation calls vary with behaviour and environment and overlap among species. We present a deep learning framework that jointly predicts species and genus and combines genus predictions with geographic species distributions at inference. When only one species of a predicted genus occurs in a region, the framework can resolve species absent from the learned taxonomy. This reframes geographic information as a means of extending, rather than constraining, a classifier's effective taxonomy. translated_title: ChiroEcho：将自动化蝙蝠叫声分类扩展到学习分类法之外
translated_abstract: 蝙蝠是生态系统健康的关键指标，并在整个欧洲受到保护，因此可靠的种群监测是保护工作的优先事项。它们隐秘的夜行生活方式使得被动声学监测成为必需，然而由于回声定位叫声随行为和环境变化，并在物种间存在重叠，自动化识别仍然困难。我们提出了一种深度学习框架，该框架联合预测物种和属，并在推理时将属的预测与地理物种分布相结合。当预测属中只有一个物种出现在某地区时，该框架能够解析出学习分类法之外的物种。这重新定义了地理信息的作用，即作为扩展分类器有效分类法的手段，而非限制因素。利用涵盖35种欧洲蝙蝠物种的录音，我们评估了封闭集分类，检查了稀疏代表物种性能估计的不稳定性，并进行了相关研究。
tldr: 该论文提出了一种深度学习框架，通过结合属级预测和地理分布信息，能够识别出训练分类法之外的蝙蝠物种，从而扩展了自动化叫声分类的适用范围。
en_tdlr: This paper presents a deep learning framework that combines genus-level predictions with geographic species distributions to identify bat species beyond the learned taxonomy, extending automated vocalization classification.
